title: HDB Wall Hacking & Demolition Permit Guide Singapore (2026)
author: Tabeeb Technical Engineering Team
excerpt: Everything you need to know about hacking walls in your HDB flat: permit requirements, load-bearing vs non-structural walls, costs, and timeline.
content:
Planning to Hack a Wall in Your HDB Flat?

Open-concept living rooms, semi-open kitchen counters, and expanded master bedrooms are among the most popular home renovation ideas in Singapore today. However, before you take a sledgehammer or rotary breaker to any wall, understanding HDB's statutory demolition guidelines is critical to prevent hefty fines, structural damage, or stop-work orders.

💡 Quick Golden Rule

Never hack any wall before obtaining the official written HDB Renovation Permit. All hacking works must be carried out by a contractor listed on the Directory of Renovations Contractors (DRC).

1. Identifying Load-Bearing Columns vs Non-Structural Walls

In HDB architecture, structural stability relies on reinforced concrete (RC) walls, pillars, and shear beams. HDB strictly strictly prohibits hacking, drilling deeply, or altering any structural element.

  • Solid RC Shear Walls / Columns (DO NOT TOUCH): Indicated on your HDB floor plan by dark, solid bold lines. These support the structural weight of the floors above you. Tampering with RC columns is illegal.
  • Non-Structural Partition Walls (Hacking Allowed with Permit): Indicated by thin or hollow lines on floor plans. These are typically lightweight concrete blockwork or drywall partitions separating rooms or closing off kitchens.

2. The HDB Hacking Permit Application Workflow

Securing approval is straightforward when working with an experienced direct contractor like Tabeeb Contractor:

  1. Blueprint Review: We inspect your official HDB floor plan to verify that the target walls are strictly non-structural.
  2. Online Submission: The licensed contractor submits an electronic permit application via the My HDBPage portal along with marked layout plans.
  3. Approval Processing: Approvals typically take between 3 to 7 working days depending on HDB branch workload.
  4. Commencement Notice: Mandatory notices must be posted outside the flat and at the lift lobby at least 3 days prior to notify neighbors of noisy hacking hours.

⚠️ Permitted Noise Hours for HDB Hacking

HDB permits heavy, noisy works (demolition, floor tile hacking, and rotary drilling) strictly from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays only. No noisy works are permitted on Saturdays, Sundays, or Public Holidays.

3. What Does HDB Hacking Typically Cost?

Hacking costs depend primarily on the length and height of the wall, whether tiles are being stripped, and haulage accessibility:

  • Standard 10-ft Non-Structural Wall Hacking: S$500 – S$900
  • Living & Dining Floor Tile Hacking (4-room HDB): S$1,600 – S$2,400
  • Kitchen & 2 Bathrooms Full Hacking (Floors & Walls): S$2,200 – S$3,500
  • Debris Haulage & Disposal to NEA Landfill: Included in comprehensive contractor quotes

title: Complete Commercial Office Reinstatement Checklist for Landlord Handover
author: Tabeeb Commercial Project Division
excerpt: Avoid forfeiture of your security deposit! Read our step-by-step commercial reinstatement guide for Singapore office, retail, and warehouse tenants.
content:
Exiting a Commercial Tenancy in Singapore?

In Singapore's commercial leasing market (CBD high-rise towers, business parks, shophouses, and industrial flatted factories), standard tenancy agreements contain strict 'Make Good' or 'Reinstatement' clauses. Tenants are legally obligated to return the leased premises back to the landlord in the exact original bare-shell condition—or face substantial deductions from their security deposit (typically 3 to 6 months of gross rental!).

📋 The Golden Handover Goal

To pass the joint landlord handover inspection on the very first walk-through and ensure 100% of your commercial tenancy deposit is refunded without delay.

1. Complete Scope Checklist for Office Reinstatements

Here is what typical commercial landlords in Singapore (such as CapitaLand, Mapletree, City Developments, and Ascendas) demand during reinstatement:

A. Partitions & Glass Demountable Walls

  • Dismantle all gypsum drywall partitions, executive suite rooms, and meeting room walls.
  • Remove frameless tempered glass partitions, sliding doors, and aluminum tracks.
  • Patch screw anchor holes in ceiling grids and perimeter perimeter columns.

B. Flooring Restoration

  • Strip all carpet tiles, vinyl flooring, or raised access flooring added during tenancy.
  • Scrape off glue residues and black mastic adhesive down to the raw concrete slab.
  • Grind and apply self-levelling screed where subfloor surfaces have suffered gouges or indentations.

C. Ceiling & Fire Safety Systems (M&E)

  • Restore the standard 600x600mm acoustic mineral fiber ceiling grid.
  • Replace any stained, sagging, or cut ceiling tiles with exact manufacturer matching models.
  • Relocate fire sprinkler heads and smoke detectors back to building baseline coverage layout according to FSSD standards.

D. Electrical & Power Infrastructure

  • Disconnect sub-distribution boards, server room UPS circuits, and supplementary power runs.
  • Remove data cabling (Cat6/Cat6A patch panels) and trunking back to telephone risers.
  • Test emergency exit signage and standard tenant lighting fixtures.

E. Painting & Finishing

  • Repaint all perimeter masonry walls with landlord-approved standard building white emulsion.
  • Ensure zero hairline cracks, anchor holes, or picture hook blemishes remain.

⏰ When to Start Your Reinstatement

Never wait until the final two weeks of your lease! Building managements require up to 7–10 days just to approve Risk Assessment / Method Statements (RAMS) and issue work permits. We recommend beginning contractor engagement 4 to 6 weeks before lease end.

title: Waterproofing & Non-Hacking PU Chemical Injection: Stop Ceiling Leaks Fast
author: Tabeeb Waterproofing Specialists
excerpt: Discover how high-pressure Polyurethane (PU) chemical injection stops bathroom ceiling leaks and inter-floor seepage without hacking expensive tiles.
content:
Ceiling Water Droplets, Peeling Paint, and Mould?

Few issues cause more household distress in high-density Singapore apartments than an inter-floor water leak. You walk into your bathroom, and water is continuously dripping from the ceiling concrete slab or down the sanitary waste pipe. The traditional solution—hacking up the upstairs neighbor's floor tiles—is loud, dirty, disruptive, and often sparks painful neighbor disputes.

Fortunately, modern structural engineering provides a proven, non-destructive alternative: High-Pressure Polyurethane (PU) Chemical Injection Grouting.

How High-Pressure PU Injection Works

Polyurethane injection grouting is a cutting-edge technique that stops active water leaks directly from the bottom (your ceiling), eliminating the requirement to hack the upper floor:

  1. Thermal Camera Diagnosis: A FLIR infrared camera scans the ceiling to map moisture patterns and trace the primary crack fissures behind the paint.
  2. 45-Degree Port Drilling: Specialized mechanical injection packers (brass ports) are drilled at an angle to intersect the water-bearing concrete fissure inside the slab.
  3. High-Pressure Hydrophobic Injection: A motorized pump forces hydrophobic liquid PU resin through the packers under 2,000+ PSI pressure deep into the interior capillaries of the slab.
  4. Expansive Reaction: As soon as the liquid resin contacts moisture, it rapidly reacts, expanding up to 25 to 30 times its volume into an impenetrable, flexible closed-cell rubber barrier that permanently seals the void.
  5. Clean Finishing: The ports are detached, holes plugged with high-strength non-shrink grout, and the ceiling is coated with anti-mould paint.

🏆 Key Advantages of PU Injection

  • Zero Hacking: Upper floor tiles and bathroom vanities remain completely undisturbed.
  • Speed: Most repairs take just 3 to 5 hours to complete.
  • Flexible Durability: PU cures into a flexible foam that withstands building vibration and thermal expansion without cracking.
  • Cost-Effective: Up to 60% cheaper than total bathroom floor hacking and re-tiling.

Is PU Injection Approved by HDB?

Yes. Under the HDB Goodwill Partner Assistance scheme for inter-floor leaks, PU chemical injection is officially recognized as an approved repair method. Tabeeb Contractor provides full documentation, before-and-after thermal reports, and written warranty coverage.

title: BCA Cement Screed vs Self-Levelling Flooring: Which Do You Need for Your Singapore Reno?
author: Tabeeb Architectural Finishing Team
excerpt: Demystifying pre-packed cement screed regulations for HDB BTOs and resale flats. Compare screeding costs, curing timelines, and tile bonding durability.
content:
The Secret Behind Perfect, Crack-Free Floors

Whether you dream of large-format Italian porcelain tiles, warm herringbone vinyl, or an industrial minimalist polished cement floor, the longevity of your flooring depends 90% on what lies beneath the surface: The Subfloor Screed.

In Singapore, many homeowners find themselves confused between terms like pre-packed cement screed, self-levelling underlayment, and bonding slurry. Here is a clear, expert breakdown from our master masonry team.

1. Why BCA Mandates Pre-Packed Cement Screed for HDB Flats

Previously, contractors mixed raw sand, water, and Portland cement on-site by eye. Inconsistent sand-to-cement ratios caused hollow tiles, uneven drying shrinkage, and brittle cracks beneath newly laid floors. To protect homeowners, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and HDB made the use of pre-packed screed compulsory for all HDB flat floors and wet areas.

  • Consistent Quality: Pre-packed screeds (like QuickMix, Davco, or Bostik) are blended in computer-controlled factories with calibrated sand grain gradation and polymer additives.
  • Superior Bonding: Pre-packed mixes demonstrate far higher tensile adhesion, drastically reducing the risk of 'popping' tiles during seasonal humidity changes.
  • Eco-Friendly: Less site dust, cleaner corridors, and lower wastage.

2. When Do You Need Self-Levelling Compound?

While cement screed is manually troweled by skilled tilers to achieve general slope and flatness, self-levelling compound is a fluid polymer-modified cementitious slurry poured onto the floor:

  • Ideal for Luxury Vinyl & SPC Flooring: Click-lock vinyl planks are thin (typically 4mm to 6mm) and unforgiving; even a 2mm dip in the floor can cause bouncy clicks or joint separation. Self-levelling ensures an optical laser-flat surface.
  • Rapid Drying: Many self-levelling compounds cure enough for foot traffic within 4 to 6 hours and can be covered with vinyl within 24 hours.

💡 Pro Renovation Tip

If you are renovating an older resale HDB flat with uneven floors, investing in a laser-checked pre-packed screed with a bonding primer coat prevents costly tile hollow sound rectifications later!
